title: Browse My Work
text:
What Does a Listing Do?
A listing collects links and descriptions into one place. Quarto can read that information from pages or from a YAML file. I used projects.yml for this site because there are only three entries to keep track of.
When I add a project to that file and render again, Quarto adds it to the table. I still need to publish the updated site for visitors to see it.

title: Browse My Work
text:
The Settings I Used
These are the main settings in this page’s header:
listing:
  id: portfolio-examples
  contents: projects.yml
  type: table
  fields: [title, description, categories]
  sort: "title"
  categories: true
contents points to my entries. type chooses the layout, and fields chooses the columns. I also renamed the column headings in the full header and turned off the search and sorting controls for this small collection.
The div named portfolio-examples puts the listing just below my introduction.

title: Browse My Work
text:
Add a Project
Here’s the dashboard entry from projects.yml:
- title: "Case 31: Credit Union Member Experience"
  path: case31-dashboard.html
  description: "Employee ratings, service awareness, and loan perceptions from the Case 31 teaching data."
  categories: [R, Survey Analysis, Quarto]
The path is the page that opens when someone clicks the title. Categories let visitors browse by skill. For example, choosing R shows the dashboard entry.

title: PhD Orthodontics: Content and Patient Information
text:
What I’m Working On
What do prospective patients want to know before contacting PhD Orthodontics? How clearly does the website answer those questions?
That’s the focus of my objective, AO3: content and lead generation. I’m looking at the information on the pages, including treatment explanations, payment information, and consultation steps. San Gabriel is our current focus. Chino Hills is a future planning area.

title: PhD Orthodontics: Content and Patient Information
text:
What I’ve Done So Far
I compared PhD Orthodontics with Valley Smiles Orthodontics and San Marino Orthodontics for our report. I also prepared and presented that comparison and the content opportunities in our proposal slides.







What I noticed in our review
What I want to check next




PhD has early-treatment information, FAQs, provider qualifications, and appointment prompts.
How clearly do the pages explain early treatment versus monitoring and what happens at a consultation?


Valley Smiles’ Alhambra page puts treatment information, financing, directions, and a consultation form together.
Can someone find PhD’s treatment, payment, and contact information without searching across several pages?


San Marino’s aligner page explains the process, and its Patient Resources page covers insurance and financing.
How fully does PhD explain the treatment process and payment options?



These examples come from our report and proposal review. They give me things to check; I haven’t confirmed that those topics are missing from PhD’s website.

title: PhD Orthodontics: Content and Patient Information
section: My Plan for the Content Audit
text:
My Plan for the Content Audit
I’ll review the relevant service, FAQ, education, financial, provider, location, and consultation pages. For each topic, I’ll save the page URL, review date, and a short excerpt or page location supporting the code.







Code
How I’ll use it




0 — Absent
An applicable topic isn’t addressed on the reviewed page.


1 — Brief
The page mentions the topic but gives little explanation.


2 — Explained
The page gives details that help answer the question.



I’ll keep clarity notes separately and check other included pages before calling something a website-wide gap. Inaccessible pages and topics that don’t apply will stay separate from a zero score. Clinical questions will go to the client for checking.
I plan to ask another member to independently review about 20% of the coding records and record agreement before we discuss differences.

title: PhD Orthodontics: Content and Patient Information
text:
What the Survey Would Add
The draft asks what information people need before showing them selected website material. People who confirm reviewing that material then rate its clarity, relevance, coverage, and usefulness. I’ll look at those items separately and keep “cannot judge” apart from neutral answers.
The open questions could show what people still want to know and what might stop them from contacting the practice. The Qualtrics export is a questionnaire draft, not response data. The website material still needs instructor confirmation, so I don’t have survey findings to report yet.

title: PhD Orthodontics: Content and Patient Information
text:
What I’d Like to Produce
I’d like to make a table linking each suggested content change to the reason for it: a question raised in the survey, a topic found in the audit, a competitor example, a review theme, or a captured search topic.
The partial Google Ads search terms can give me topics to check. They don’t show overall search demand or which content led to an inquiry. I’ll use the audit and survey evidence to decide the priorities with the team.

title: Case 31: Credit Union Dashboard
text:
What’s Inside







Page
What you’ll find




Member Experience
Employee ratings, overall ratings, loan status, and rate perceptions


Service Awareness
Awareness and use of 14 credit union services


Data Notes
The source, response scales, and how I handled missing answers



The workbook has 128 records. The average employee rating is 4.21 out of 5. For the overall management and operation question, 102 of 121 valid answers (84.3%) are good or excellent.
Those overall results look positive, but the employee chart shows that availability has lower agreement than courtesy or helpfulness. I’d want to ask about that difference before suggesting a change.






NoteA quick note on the scales



A higher employee rating is favorable. A higher borrowing-rate score means someone thinks the rate is high. They answer different questions, so I show them separately.

title: Case 31: Credit Union Dashboard
text:
How I Put It Together
I read the Excel file with read_excel(), then used pivot_longer(), count(), and summarise() to prepare the chart data. I made the plots with ggplot2 and the tables with knitr::kable().
The dashboard uses headings for its pages and rows, value boxes for the main numbers, and tabs for the extra detail. The code runs when I render the file. Visitors can switch pages and tabs in the HTML output.

title: Case 31: Credit Union Dashboard
text:
About the Data
These are course teaching data, separate from my CEP. I used the prepared columns and the instructor’s coding notes. The dashboard’s Data Notes explain missing answers and a difference between the workbook’s record count and the count described in the printed case.
Source: Jae Min Jung, Employees Federal Credit Union Case, CC BY 4.0. I adapted the prepared data into this dashboard.

title: How I Styled This Site
text:
I started with Quarto’s Cosmo theme and added teal links, a navy navigation bar, and a light background. I also made a note style and a small project card. You can see both examples on this page.
HTML gives a page its structure. CSS controls how it looks, including the colors, fonts, borders, and spacing. SCSS lets me use variables and nest related rules. Quarto turns that SCSS into CSS when I render the site.

title: How I Styled This Site
text:
Load the Style Files
These settings in _quarto.yml apply to the regular website pages:
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, site.scss]
    css: styles.css
site.scss changes the theme. styles.css adds a few rules for particular parts of the page. The dashboard loads dashboard.scss in its own header because it has a different layout.
